fatal_errors: The proposed material and intervention—laser-peened 304L stainless steel—do not reconstruct the target system of an annealed atmospheric-plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating on SS316L.

The stated 1% NaCl environment applies to the cited impedance test, whereas the cited intergranular-corrosion tests used 0.5 M H2SO4 plus KSCN or boiling 65% HNO3; combining these as one study condition obscures which outcome each environment tests.

The experiment does not independently vary or quantify residual stress, grain refinement, dislocation density, and roughness, so it cannot identify compressive residual stress as the governing cause rather than a correlated peening-induced change.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative hypothesis rather than a reconstruction of the hidden target. It addresses corrosion resistance in an application-relevant stainless steel, provides an untreated baseline, measurable electrochemical and intergranular-corrosion outcomes, and cites directly relevant findings that laser peening creates compressive stress and changes microstructure. However, it disagrees with the target in alloy, coating, processing route, annealing conditions, corrosive environments, passive-film mechanism, and hot-corrosion outcomes. Its causal claim is also stronger than the proposed comparison can establish: laser peening simultaneously changes residual stress, roughness, grain size, hardness, and dislocation density. A stronger design would include stress-relieved peened specimens, roughness-matched controls, residual-stress depth profiles, and mediation analysis relating those variables to corrosion response. The falsification rule is too permissive because failure to improve corrosion resistance—not only significantly worse resistance—would contradict the stated directional hypothesis.
